cs.t: I bought from Newegg both times. The first time it was an ASRock MB that was dead, and to be fair, the issue here was that some part was on backorder so by the time everything arrived and I put it together I had to deal with ASRock RMA rather than the Newegg returns department. Typically I choose pretty high end components as well, I do Corsair PSUs & RAM, Samsung SSD, ASUS GPU. Definitely learned my lesson on the MB and went with ASUS for the latest build as well... though that MB's DIMM_B slot was dead. I'm just glad I ended up getting 2x16G of RAM right away instead of starting with 1x16 like I originally planned, because I would have never realized the problem until getting the second stick
cs.th: All memory manufactured in 2027 has been sold out

cs.t: This is weird. I have used many ASUS MBs specified as "can run ECC and non-ECC" and this has always meant that there was an ECC enabling option in the BIOS settings, and then if the OS had an appropriate EDAC driver for the installed CPU ECC worked fine. I am writing this message on such an ASUS MB with a Ryzen CPU and working ECC memory. You must check that you actually have a recent enough OS to know your Threadripper CPU and that you have installed any software package required for this (e.g. on Linux "edac-utils" or something with a similar name).
cs.th: I am giving up on Intel and have bought an AMD Ryzen 9950X3D
